historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: US housing starts roughly flat plus 2-3% ASP/mix inflation; the equity CAGR (14.6%) is retained peak-cycle earnings net of buybacks and is not a repeatable revenue growth rate for a cyclical already past its FY2024 earnings peak
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 14.6% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 9.4% and from EPS 3yr CAGR 0.4%; FY2025 EPS is already below FY2022. Owner-FCF CAGRs are meaningless on their endpoints: FY2022 was an inventory-build trough (owner FCF ~$490M on NI $2.6B) so the 3yr figure is 49%, while the 5yr figure is -0.5%. Neither is used for projection.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes - interest income, FY2020 ~1,668, FY2022 ~490, FY2025 1,625. Reported and owner FCF CAGRs are within 3pp of each other: SBC is ~0.5% of revenue and is not where the growth is being paid for. Cash conversion, not SBC, is the swing: cumulative FY2016-25 reported FCF was 69% of net income because inventory absorbed ~70% of revenue growth.

scenario_narratives.base: The housing cycle has turned from the FY2024 peak but does not break. Mortgage rates stay 6-6.5% through 2027, incentives remain ~10-11% of price so gross margin sits at 24.5-25% (the FY2026 guide) and SG&A at 9-9.5%; FY2026 revenue falls ~7.5% to ~$16.0B at the guided 28,500-29,000 closings and FY2027 drifts another 3% as ASP erodes. From FY2028 the +8% community-count growth and structural undersupply lift closings 3-5%/yr and the unlevered margin recovers to a 17.5% mid-cycle, below the 10-year average because FY2021-24 was a supply-shock regime but above the ~15% pre-COVID norm on consolidation, Del Webb mix and a leaner SG&A ratio. Land investment ahead of revenue keeps FY2026-27 FCF well below earnings, as in FY2025 and H1-2026, then cash conversion normalises to ~85% of NOPAT at 3% growth. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rates ease toward 5.5% in 2027 and the affordability logjam loosens: incentives fall from ~11% to ~6% of price, gross margin recovers toward 27-28%, SG&A leverages to ~8.5%, and the order growth already visible in Q2 2026 (+6% units, +5% value on +8% communities) converts to 6-7% closings growth in FY2028-29. Del Webb's less rate-sensitive 55+ buyer and the build-to-order mix shift protect margin through the transition, and scale consolidation lets the top builders take share from private builders squeezed on land and labor. Mid-cycle margin settles at 19.5%, which is still 4pp below FY2022-24; that regime is not assumed to return even here. Revenue reaches ~$23.8B by FY2035.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2027 recession with rising unemployment hits an already affordability-strained buyer. Closings fall ~9% in FY2026 (below the guided range), 12% in FY2027 and 6% in FY2028; price cuts and incentives push gross margin to 19-20%, SG&A delevers to 12% on a smaller base, and owned land bought at FY2023-25 cost assumptions is impaired. The unlevered margin troughs at 9% in FY2028 and recovers only to the ~15% pre-COVID norm, with revenue still below FY2025 in FY2035. Inventory liquidation releases cash through the trough (as it did for PHM in 2008-09), which is what keeps this bear from being a solvency event: debt-to-capital is 12%, the nearest senior-note maturity is small, and the balance sheet carries $13B of inventory at cost.

valuation_philosophy.summary: PulteGroup is valued as a cyclical operating company on owner FCF with explicit mid-cycle normalisation rather than by extrapolating FY2024 peak earnings. The flows are unlevered (capitalized interest added back, interest income stripped) so the $485M of net debt is deducted exactly once; SBC is expensed and the count held flat; land investment is charged through a negative working-capital capture on revenue growth plus a front-loaded land-ahead-of-revenue capex line, which is what reconciles the model to PulteGroup's actual 69% ten-year cash conversion. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, with a single 10% USD WACC and a 12x terminal cap appropriate to a sector that has never sustained a premium multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of terminal unlevered margin is worth roughly $8-9/share; the 17.5% base sits between the ~15% pre-COVID norm and the 18.5% ten-year average and could be wrong in either direction
Land cash conversion: if community-count growth keeps land spend ahead of revenue beyond FY2028, FCF stays well below NOPAT and the Y4-Y10 capex taper is too generous
Mortgage-rate path: the base assumes 6-6.5% through 2027; a move to 7%+ puts the bear path in play and a move to 5.5% the bull path
Terminal cap: 12x owner FCF is a judgment; the Gordon value at 10%/2.5% is 13.7x and the stock's own history supports 8-12x earnings

Impairments in the bear case reduce book inventory rather than cash and are not separately modelled; the bear relies on inventory liquidation generating cash, which assumes homes still clear at lower prices
Financial Services warehouse borrowings are treated as operating and excluded from debt; a secondary-market disruption would change that

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 108.49-144.50
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 822416): FY2025 10-K filed 2026-02-04 for FY0 flows; Q2 2026 10-Q filed 2026-07-22 for notes payable, cash, shares and H1-2026 flows; PHM_Metrics.csv for the FY2008-Q2 2026 history; kpis table for buybacks, cash taxes, D&A, equity-award taxes
data_sources.qualitative: PHM_Analysis.json 2026-10-02 (FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at Q2 2026: 28,500-29,000 closings, 24.5-25.0% gross margin, 9.0-9.5% SG&A; incentives ~10.9% of price; $2.2B buyback authorization) and the Q2 2026 earnings release (EX-99.1, 8-K 2026-07-22: 6,997 closings, ASP $544k, GM 25.0%, SG&A 10.1%, orders +6%, backlog $6.8B, $373M repurchased)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 187.453M cover-page shares at 2026-07-15 (Q2 2026 10-Q) plus the 1.195M Q2 2026 dilutive-securities adjustment (190.583M diluted less 189.388M basic weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the ~$1.2-1.4B/yr buyback is a distribution of the same FCF the model values and is value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation $54.8M plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $24.3M, summed because PulteGroup publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure
inputs.debt_detail: Senior notes $1,782.9M + other notes payable $37.4M = $1,820.3M at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q, us-gaap:NotesPayable). Financial Services warehouse/repo borrowings are excluded: they fund $562.4M of mortgage loans held for sale and both are operating items. The Metrics.csv TotalDebt column (31-74) is the XBRL LongTermDebt tag, which is not the notes balance; do not use it. Cash $1,335.7M is unrestricted only (restricted $41.6M excluded). Buybacks since 30 June (~$350M/qtr) lower both cash and count roughly value-neutrally.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. 10y UST ~4.1% + homebuilder beta ~1.35 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.9% cost of equity; debt ~12% of capital at ~5.0% pre-tax / 3.8% after tax; WACC = 10.0%. Same WACC in every scenario; cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$150M liabilities): lease expense is already inside SG&A and therefore inside the EBITDA margin (treatment B); lease liabilities excluded from net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path needed.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests immaterial; flows are attributable. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.working_capital_note: A homebuilder's capital is inventory (~$13.5B of house and land inventory against $17B revenue, ~0.75x). Over FY2016-25 inventory absorbed ~70% of each revenue dollar added and cumulative reported FCF was 69% of cumulative net income during 9%/yr revenue growth. wc_capture_pct is therefore NEGATIVE (growth consumes cash, decline releases it): -55% base/bull, -40% bear (slower turnover and spec build-up blunt the release in a recession). Because PulteGroup keeps investing in land for community-count growth (+8% YoY) even while revenue falls (FY2025 absorbed ~$0.5B; H1-2026 FCF $121M on NI $819M), capex_pct_path in Y1-Y3 carries net land investment ahead of revenue on top of ~0.7% PP&E capex, tapering to PP&E only from Y4 when revenue-driven working capital alone carries the land charge.
inputs.margin_calibration: ebitda_margin_path is UNLEVERED adjusted EBITDA before SBC: pretax income + D&A + interest amortized through cost of sales (homebuilders capitalize interest into inventory: $122.1M FY2025, $53.4M H1-2026) - interest income + SBC. FY2016 14.7%, FY2017 13.5%, FY2018 15.6%, FY2019 15.6%, FY2020 18.1%, FY2021 20.2%, FY2022 23.1%, FY2023 22.7%, FY2024 23.4%, FY2025 18.2%, H1-2026 16.0%. Pre-COVID normal ~15%, 10-year average 18.5% inflated by the FY2021-24 supply-shock regime. Base mid-cycle set at 17.5%: credit for consolidation, Del Webb mix and a 9-9.5% SG&A ratio vs 10%+ pre-COVID, but not for 2021-24 margins. Adding back capitalized interest is what makes deducting net debt once correct.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle normalisation (dcf-methods routing: cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. FY0 = FY2025; Y1 = FY2026, of which H1 is reported (revenue -11%, NI -28% YoY) and FY guidance (28,500-29,000 closings, 24.5-25.0% gross margin, 9.0-9.5% SG&A) implies ~-7.5% revenue. Peak-cycle FY2024 (23.4% margin, $14.82 EPS) is deliberately NOT the base: every scenario troughs in FY2026-28 and recovers to a stated mid-cycle margin by Y6. Owner FCF (last_fcf) = reported FCF 1,748.5 - SBC incl. equity taxes 79.2 - interest income 44.4 = 1,624.9. Interest income is stripped (and cash held at face in the bridge) even though net cash is not >1x FCF, because the forward build is unlevered via the capitalized-interest add-back and consistency requires both sides of the financing to leave the flows. Buybacks: $1.2B FY2025 and $681M H1-2026 of actual financing-activity outflow, so the flat count is funded many times over. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF in all scenarios (cyclical; peers' long-run P/E 8-12x) binds below Gordon at 10%/2.5%, so terminal-growth sensitivity is muted by design. Street basis differs from house by only ~0.5% of revenue of SBC; the band is narrow. Part of Y1 FCF is already inside the June balance sheet (~$0.6/share); accepted.

bear.growth_rationale: A 2027 recession with job losses: FY2026 misses the low end of guidance (-9%), FY2027 -12%, FY2028 -6%; revenue troughs at ~$13.0B (-25% from FY2025, far milder than the -75% of 2006-09 given today's undersupply and balance sheets) and recovers slowly to ~$16.0B by FY2035.
bear.margin_rationale: Gross margin compresses to ~19-20% on price cuts and incentives, SG&A delevers to 12%, land impairments hit FY2027-28; unlevered EBITDA margin troughs at 9% and recovers only to 15% (the pre-COVID normal) because the 2021-24 margins prove to have been a one-off.
bear.wc_rationale: Inventory liquidation does generate cash in a downturn (PHM OCF was +$1.2B in 2008), but turnover slows and spec inventory builds, so the release per revenue dollar lost is set at 40% rather than 55%.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at guidance (28,750 closings x ~$540k ASP + ~$0.45B financial services/land = ~$16.0B, -7.5%); FY2027 -3% as backlog value is -1% YoY and ASP keeps drifting down on incentives; recovery FY2028-31 as community count (+8% YoY) converts to closings and rates ease modestly; 2.5-3% nominal thereafter.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 16.3% (H1 actual 16.0%, H2 SG&A leverage toward the 9-9.5% guide); FY2027 trough 15.8% as incentives stay 10%+; recovery to 17.5% mid-cycle by FY2031 and held.
base.capex_rationale: Y1 8.0% = ~0.7% PP&E + ~$1.2B land investment ahead of revenue (land spend continuing while revenue falls, as in FY2025/H1-2026); Y2 4.5%, Y3 2.0%, then PP&E only with wc_capture carrying revenue-driven land.

bull.growth_rationale: Mortgage rates fall toward 5.5% in 2027, incentives taper, the +6% order growth and +8% community count turn into closings growth from FY2027; revenue reaches ~$23.8B by FY2035 (3.2% CAGR off FY2025).
bull.margin_rationale: Incentives fall from ~11% to ~6% of price, gross margin recovers toward 27-28% with SG&A ~8.5%; mid-cycle 19.5%, still 4pp below the FY2022-24 regime, which is not assumed to return.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because homebuilding is at the most rate-sensitive point of a cycle that has already turned (incentives 10-11% of price, revenue -11% in H1-2026, Q3 margin guide shows no inflection) and a recession scenario is live rather than tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right, lower mortgage rates and margin re-expansion with incentives tapering, and the order growth it leans on is off easy comps. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was reaffirmed at Q2 and the balance sheet (12% debt-to-capital, $1.3B cash) lets management execute it.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
